In VIM, I have a scrolloff = 4 line in my vimrc and it offsets my cursor from the bottom/top of the document. This means that my cursor is NEVER within four lines of the top or bottom of my document. This is nice, since I can read around my cursor. I can use N or n to search the previous or next results of my search, and they're never the first or last line on my screen.

But this isn't the case for man when I search. Try to use man mail and search for "SYSTEM" with /SYSTEM and hit enter. The word "SYSTEM" is in the last line of a section, so in order to know that it's part of the -n option, you'll have to scroll up several lines... and to even read the sentence it's a part of, you'll still have to scroll up a few lines.

Now, I know that this is all relevant to how wide I keep my terminal window, but there will ALWAYS be a search command that's too far into a description, and you'll ALWAYS have to scroll to read.
